mainTopic: When an עירוב takes effect; the conditional עירוב (מתנה אדם על עירובו) and רבי יהודה's view of ברירה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about when an עירוב takes effect: at the start of שבת (תחילת היום) or at the last moment of Friday (סוף היום). רב פפא rejects the proof for סוף היום, because the עירוב food must be edible while it is still Friday anyway. A new משנה then teaches that a person may make his עירוב conditional. Which direction counts can depend on whether גוים come from one side, or whether a חכם comes from one side. רבי יהודה adds that if one of two חכמים is his own רבי, he must go to his רבי. The גמרא resolves a reversed version of the משנה by explaining that it speaks about different kinds of גוים and different kinds of חכמים. It also explains that the רבנן let him choose because a person sometimes prefers a colleague over his teacher. רב then rejects the משנה's report of רבי יהודה, relying on איו's ברייתא, in which רבי יהודה does not allow a condition on two חכמים at once because of אין ברירה. רבי יוחנן explains that the one-חכם case is not ברירה, because the חכם had already arrived. The גמרא begins proving that רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה from a case of wine bought from the כותים, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proving the עירוב takes effect at the end of Friday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if an עירוב took effect at the start of שבת, the food in this case should be valid. Since the earlier ruling says it is invalid, the עירוב must take effect at the end of Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think the beginning of the day (שבת) is what acquires the עירוב, then when he said 'make an עירוב for me with this,' why does the ruling say he said nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument from an earlier case. In that case, food became usable only once שבת began, and the ruling was that 'he said nothing,' meaning the עירוב is not valid. The גמרא uses this to prove that the עירוב takes effect at the end of Friday (סוף היום).
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start of שבת the food was already fit to eat. So if the עירוב took hold then, it should work. Since the ruling says it does not work, the moment of acquisition must be the end of Friday, when the food was still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind / you might think
The beginning of the day, meaning the start of שבת
The עירוב acquires (sets) one's שבת residence
He said nothing, meaning his act has no effect

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind
that the beginning of the day acquires the eiruv,
then if he said: Make an eiruv for me with this,
phrases.notes: Refers to the earlier case, where the food only became usable at nightfall.

phrases.english: why has he not said anything (why is it invalid)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud, which argued that סוף היום קונה עירוב.
steps.raayaObject: That an עירוב takes effect at the end of Friday (סוף היום קונה עירוב).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier ruling that 'ערבו לי בזה' with food that is permitted only from nightfall is 'לא אמר כלום'.

steps.title: רב פפא: The food must be edible while it is still day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof. Even if the עירוב takes effect at the start of שבת, the food must already be edible on Friday, and here it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even if you say the beginning of the day acquires the עירוב, we still need a meal that is fit to eat while it is still day, and here there isn't one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the proof from Step 1. He gives a different reason why the עירוב in that case is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case does not show anything about the moment of acquisition. There is a separate requirement: the עירוב food must be fit to eat before שבת begins. This food was forbidden on Friday, so it fails that requirement under either view.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: a rejection formula meaning 'even under your opposing view'
We require
A meal that is fit (to be eaten)
While it is still day (before שבת)
And there is none

steps.whatToRemember: The question of תחילת היום vs. סוף היום stays unproven from this case. That is because the עירוב food must be edible already on Friday (ראויה מבעוד יום).
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the עירוב takes effect at the start of שבת. He only shows that this case cannot decide the question.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא תְּחִילַּת הַיּוֹם קוֹנֶה עֵירוּב,
phrases.english: Even if you say the beginning of the day acquires the eiruv,
we still require a meal fit to eat while it is still day,
and there is none here.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only. It does not rule out סוף היום.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The invalidity can be explained by the separate requirement that the food be edible on Friday.

steps.title: משנה: A conditional עירוב based on where גוים come from
steps.stepSummary: A person may place עירובין in two directions. He can make the one that counts depend on which direction גוים come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may put a condition on his עירוב and say: If גוים come from the east, my עירוב is in the west. If from the west, my עירוב is in the east. If they come from both sides, I will go wherever I want. If they come from neither side, I am like the people of my town.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a person can make his עירוב conditional, so its direction is decided by later events, here the threat of attacking גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He places an עירוב on two sides of town. Which one is valid depends on events, so he can flee in the safe direction. If no one comes, he gives up both עירובין and keeps the normal 2,000 אמות around the town.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
A person may make a condition on his עירוב
Gentiles (here, a threatening force)
To here and to there: from both directions
Like the people of my town (the regular תחום)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an עירוב's direction can be left open and settled later by a condition. The גמרא will later connect this to the concept of ברירה (retroactive clarification).

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may make a condition on his eiruv,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: אִם בָּאוּ גּוֹיִם מִן הַמִּזְרָח —
phrases.english: and say: If gentiles come from the east,
my eiruv is to the west.
If from the west, my eiruv is to the east.
If they come from here and from there,
I will go to whichever place I want.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּאוּ לֹא לְכָאן וְלֹא לְכָאן —
phrases.english: If they did not come, neither from here nor from there,
I am like the people of my town.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב may be made conditional on future events, such as the direction from which גוים come.

steps.title: משנה: A conditional עירוב based on where a חכם comes from
steps.stepSummary: The same kind of condition can depend on which direction a חכם comes from, so he can go greet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a חכם comes from the east, my עירוב is to the east. If from the west, my עירוב is to the west. If one comes from each side, I will go wherever I want. If none comes, I am like the people of my town.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of a conditional עירוב. This time the purpose is to go toward a visiting חכם, not to run away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the direction flips compared to Step 3. With גוים you go the opposite way; with a חכם you go the same way, toward him. The legal mechanism of the condition is identical.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar
I will go wherever I want

phrases.english: If a Sage comes from the east,
my eiruv is to the east.
If from the west, my eiruv is to the west.
If one came from here and from there,
I will go to whichever place I want.
If neither from here nor from there,
I am like the people of my town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second case within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב may be conditioned on the direction from which a חכם arrives.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: If one of the Sages is his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the choice. If one of the two חכמים is his רבי, he must go to his רבי. If both are his teachers, he may choose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If one of them was his teacher, he goes to his teacher. If both were his teachers, he may go wherever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit to the case of two חכמים coming from both sides. He disagrees with the free choice the תנא קמא allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, we assume the person's real intention all along was to greet his own רבי. So he cannot pick the other חכם. Free choice applies only when both are his teachers, since then neither is clearly preferred.

keyTerms.meaning: His teacher
His teachers
To / toward

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows a conditional עירוב (for גוים or a חכם). In a case with two חכמים, the תנא קמא allows free choice. רבי יהודה requires going to one's own רבי, unless both are his teachers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one of them was his teacher,
he goes to his teacher,
and if both of them were his teachers,
he may go to whichever place he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the free choice given in Step 4 when two חכמים come.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one חכם is his רבי, he must go to him. If both are his teachers, he may choose.

steps.title: רבי יצחק teaches the whole משנה in reverse
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יצחק came from ארץ ישראל, he taught every ruling in the משנה the opposite way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: When רבי יצחק came, he taught the whole משנה in reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by reporting a different version of our משנה. In רבי יצחק's version, every ruling is flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our version, if גוים come from one side, the person's עירוב counts on the other side, so he can get away from them. If a חכם comes from one side, his עירוב counts on that side, so he can go meet him. רבי יצחק taught the reverse, which sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The opposite, in reverse
Our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק is not giving a new opinion. He is reporting a different version of the same משנה, and the rulings in that version are flipped.

phrases.english: Gemara: When Rabbi Yitzchak came
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a different version of the text.

phrases.english: he taught the whole Mishnah in reverse.
phrases.notes: Every ruling in the משנה is flipped.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק תָּנֵי אִיפְּכָא כּוּלָּהּ מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate, reversed reading of the משנה rulings stated in steps 3 to 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יצחק's version, every directional ruling of the משנה is reversed.

steps.title: The two versions now contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two versions now clash, both about גוים and about a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: the ruling about גוים contradicts the other ruling about גוים, and the ruling about a חכם contradicts the other ruling about a חכם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with having two opposite versions. One says to go toward the גוים, and the other says to go away from them. The same clash exists for the חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions cannot be right if they describe the same situation. The גמרא is asking how both can be legitimate teachings. This sets up the two answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; this is a contradiction
The ruling about גוים against the other ruling about גוים
The ruling about a חכם against the other ruling about a חכם

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between gentiles and gentiles,
phrases.notes: One version has him go toward the גוים, and the other has him go away from them.

phrases.english: there is a contradiction between Sage and Sage!
phrases.notes: One version has him go toward the חכם, and the other has him go away.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא גּוֹיִם אַגּוֹיִם, קַשְׁיָא חָכָם אַחָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יצחק's reversed version clashes with the standard version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two opposite versions of the rulings about גוים and about a חכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two versions that give opposite rulings for the same case cannot both be correct.

steps.title: Different kinds of gentiles: a tax collector versus the town lord
steps.stepSummary: The גוים in the two versions are different people. A person runs away from a tax collector but wants to meet the lord of the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between the rulings about גוים is not difficult. This version is about a tax collector, and that version is about the lord of the town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction. The two versions are talking about two different kinds of גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one wants to meet a tax collector, so the person sets his עירוב to get away from him. A town lord can help him, so he sets his עירוב to go toward him. The rule is the same in both versions: the עירוב follows what the person actually wants.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one… that one (two different cases)
A tax collector, someone a person wants to avoid
The lord or ruler of the town, someone a person wants to meet

phrases.english: Gentiles against gentiles is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The answer to the first contradiction.

phrases.english: this one is about a tax collector,
phrases.notes: The person wants to run away from him.

phrases.english: that one is about the lord of the town.
phrases.notes: The person wants to go and speak with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): each version describes a different type of גוי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both versions seemed to describe the same גוים, so their rulings clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: One version means a tax collector, whom he flees. The other means the town lord, whom he wants to meet.

steps.title: Different kinds of teachers: a public lecturer versus a teacher of children
steps.stepSummary: The חכם in the two versions are different people. One gives public Torah lectures, which the person wants to attend. The other only teaches children קריאת שמע, which the person does not need.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between the rulings about a חכם is not difficult. This version is about someone who gives public lectures, and that version is about someone who teaches children to read שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction in the same way. The two versions are talking about two different kinds of teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person wants to go and learn from a חכם who gives public lectures, so his עירוב goes toward him. A teacher who only teaches children קריאת שמע has nothing to offer him, so his עירוב does not go toward that teacher. Here too, the עירוב follows what the person actually wants.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sits and gives public Torah lectures
One who teaches children to read קריאת שמע

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers follow one principle. When an עירוב depends on a condition, it goes in the direction the person truly wants, toward someone useful and away from someone harmful or unneeded.

phrases.english: Sage against Sage is not difficult:
phrases.notes: The answer to the second contradiction.

phrases.english: this one is about one who sits and gives lectures,
phrases.notes: The person wants to go and learn from him.

phrases.english: that one is about one who teaches the reading of Shema.
phrases.notes: A teacher of young children, whom the person does not need.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction from step 7, using the same method as step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): each version describes a different type of חכם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both versions seemed to describe the same חכם, so their rulings clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: One version means a public lecturer, whom he goes toward. The other means a teacher of children, whom he does not need.

steps.title: Why don't the Rabbis accept רבי יהודה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה and asks what the רבנן's reasoning is for disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If one of them was his רבי, and so on. And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה, that a person must go to his own רבי. It asks why the רבנן do not accept this, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule seems obvious, since a person surely wants to greet his own teacher. So it is puzzling that the רבנן let the person choose either חכם. The single word "וְרַבָּנַן" is the question: what is their reasoning?

keyTerms.meaning: And so on; the rest of the quote is understood
And the רבנן? (a short way of asking for their reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: "וְרַבָּנַן" is a whole question packed into one word. It means: what is the reasoning of the רבנן, who disagree with רבי יהודה?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says
if one of them was his teacher, etc.
phrases.notes: Then he may only go to his רבי.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reasoning?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אִם הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְכוּ׳. וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's ruling from step 5 and asks for the reasoning of the opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן do not require the person to go to his own רבי.

steps.title: Sometimes a person prefers his colleague over his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that sometimes a person would rather meet his colleague than his teacher, so we cannot assume he meant his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes a person prefers his colleague more than his רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The רבנן believe a person does not always want to go to his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה assumes a person always wants his own רבי most. The רבנן say this is not always true, because sometimes a person gains more from a colleague. Since we cannot be sure what he wanted, they let him choose.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
He prefers it; it pleases him
His colleague or peer
More than his teacher

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about what a person most likely wants. רבי יהודה assumes it is always his רבי. The רבנן say it might be his colleague, so he may choose.

phrases.english: Sometimes he prefers his colleague
phrases.notes: A person may learn more from a peer.

phrases.english: more than his teacher.
phrases.notes: So we cannot assume he meant his רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּחַבְרֵיהּ טְפֵי מֵרַבֵּיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן hold that a person sometimes prefers his colleague over his teacher, so his intention cannot be assumed.

steps.title: רב says the משנה's version cannot be relied on
steps.stepSummary: רב states that the משנה's version of רבי יהודה's opinion is not reliable, because איו taught a different version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The משנה is not reliable here, because of what איו taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב makes a bold statement: we should not rely on the משנה's wording of רבי יהודה's opinion. This step sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes איו's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה seems to allow a person to choose between two directions after the fact. רב says another source, the ברייתא of איו, reports רבי יהודה differently. So רב sides with the ברייתא over the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not so; this version is not accepted
Our משנה
A תנא (Sage) who taught a ברייתא
Because of what was taught

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the משנה is 'wrong' in general. He is saying its report of רבי יהודה's opinion here should not be relied on, because another reliable source reports it differently.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The mishna is not [to be relied on]
because of what Ayo taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֵיתָא לְמַתְנִיתִין מִדְּתָנֵי אַיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the רבנן's reasoning, the גמרא now brings רב, who questions whether the משנה's version of רבי יהודה is accurate at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's version of רבי יהודה is not accepted, because of איו's ברייתא.

steps.title: איו's ברייתא: no condition on two things at once
steps.stepSummary: איו's ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: a person can make an עירוב conditional on which direction one חכם comes from, but not on two חכמים coming from two directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: For איו taught: רבי יהודה says a person cannot make a condition on two things at once. Instead, he may say: if a חכם comes to the east, my עירוב is to the east, and if a חכם comes to the west, my עירוב is to the west. But if חכמים come from here and from there, the condition does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source רב relies on. In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה allows the 'one חכם, unknown direction' case but rejects the 'two חכמים, I will choose later' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהודה seems to allow a choice when חכמים come from both sides. In איו's version, רבי יהודה forbids exactly that case. This contradiction is why רב rejects the משנה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a condition
Two things at once
His עירוב (his שבת base)
To here and to here; both directions

phrases.english: For Ayo taught:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person cannot make a condition
about two things at once.
Rather: if a Sage came to the east,
his eiruv is to the east;
and if a Sage came to the west,
his eiruv is to the west.
But [if Sages came] to here and to here,
no [the condition does not work].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that רב relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the משנה's version of רבי יהודה is not reliable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איו's ברייתא, where רבי יהודה rejects a condition on two חכמים coming from two sides.

steps.title: Why should east-or-west work if there is no retroactive choice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges איו's ברייתא: if the two-חכמים case fails because of אין ברירה, the one-חכם, east-or-west case should fail too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about 'here and here' that it does not work? Because there is no ברירה. But then 'east or west' should also fail, since there is no ברירה there either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an inconsistency inside איו's ברייתא. Both cases seem to depend on deciding afterward which עירוב counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the 'two חכמים' case fails must be אין ברירה: we cannot clarify after the fact what was already in effect when שבת began. But in the 'one חכם, east or west' case, the person also only finds out later which עירוב he wanted. So the same rule should invalidate that case too.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
There is no retroactive clarification. Something undecided cannot later be treated as having been decided from the start.
Also

steps.confusionAlert: ברירה does not mean 'choice' in the everyday sense. It means retroactive clarification: treating something decided later as if it had been settled from the beginning.

phrases.english: What is different about 'here and here' that it does not work?
Because there is no retroactive clarification.
[Then in the case of] east or west,
there is also no retroactive clarification!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the internal consistency of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: איו's ברייתא, which allows the east-or-west case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אין ברירה invalidates the two-חכמים case, it should equally invalidate the east-or-west case, which also depends on clarifying the situation later.

steps.title: The Sage had already arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that in the east-or-west case, the חכם had already arrived before שבת began, so there is no retroactive clarification.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The חכם had already come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. In the east-or-west case, the facts were already settled by the start of שבת. The person just did not know them yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברירה is only a problem when the deciding fact does not yet exist when שבת begins. In the east-or-west case, the חכם had already arrived at one side, so the correct עירוב was fixed. The person only learns it later. In the two-חכמים case, the person has not yet chosen, so that would need real ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he had already come

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a key distinction: a fact that is already true but unknown is not a ברירה problem. Only a decision that has not yet been made is.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And the Sage had already come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּכְבָר בָּא חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by redefining the east-or-west case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case redefinition: the deciding fact already existed at nightfall.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases depend on clarifying things later, so both should fail under אין ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the east-or-west case the חכם had already arrived, so the fact was fixed and only unknown. This is not ברירה. The two-חכמים case depends on a choice not yet made, which is ברירה.

steps.title: Why not reject איו's ברייתא instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: why reject the משנה because of the ברייתא? Maybe we should reject איו's ברייתא because of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Let us say איו's teaching is not reliable, because of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's original statement. A משנה is usually the stronger source, so why should it give way to a ברייתא? This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will need to defend רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב preferred איו's ברייתא over the משנה. The גמרא flips this: the משנה has more authority, so the ברייתא should be the one rejected. Now רב's position needs a defense.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
That of איו (his ברייתא)

phrases.english: On the contrary!
Let Ayo's [teaching] not be accepted, because of the mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the logic inside איו's ברייתא, the גמרא returns to challenge רב's choice to prefer it over the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the משנה is not reliable because of איו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה normally carries more authority than a ברייתא, so the ברייתא should give way to the משנה, not the other way around.

steps.title: We already know רבי יהודה rejects retroactive clarification
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב. The משנה's version of רבי יהודה must be the one rejected, because elsewhere רבי יהודה clearly holds אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't even think that we should keep the משנה's version, because we have heard that רבי יהודה does not hold of ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 16. It explains why רב threw out the משנה's version and kept איו's ברייתא, and not the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's version has רבי יהודה allowing a choice that only becomes clear later, which would mean he accepts ברירה. But we have an independent source showing that רבי יהודה does not accept ברירה. איו's ברייתא fits that source, so it wins and the משנה's version is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind; that idea is unthinkable
We have heard him (say); we know his position from elsewhere
Retroactive clarification: a later event reveals what was chosen earlier
He does not hold of (this principle)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting a משנה lightly. It rejects only the משנה's report of רבי יהודה's opinion, because that report clashes with his known view on ברירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key method in the גמרא. When two sources quote the same תנא differently, we keep the version that matches his views elsewhere.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind (to keep the mishna's version),
for we have heard regarding Rabbi Yehuda
that he does not hold of retroactive clarification.
phrases.notes: This means he holds אין ברירה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּהָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 16 by explaining why the משנה, and not the ברייתא, must give way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to the תנא's established position elsewhere, which settles which conflicting version is authentic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the משנה's version is correct and איו's ברייתא should be rejected instead.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה is known to hold אין ברירה, so the משנה's version, which implies ברירה, is the one rejected.

steps.title: The proof begins: buying wine from the כותים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the source that shows רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה: the case of someone who buys wine from the כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one who buys wine from among the כותים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof for Step 17. It starts quoting a teaching from מסכת דמאי, and the case finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים were not trusted to separate מעשרות properly, so wine bought from them may still need its מעשרות taken off. The rest of this case will show how רבי יהודה treats a later designation of those portions, and that will prove his view on ברירה. At this point only the opening of the case is given.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys
Samaritans, who were not trusted to separate מעשרות properly

phrases.english: As we learned: one who buys wine
from among the Samaritans,
phrases.notes: The case continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind Step 17's claim that רבי יהודה does not hold of ברירה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching in מסכת דמאי about one who buys wine from the כותים (the case continues on the next amud)
